value.first: I'd start with the 3-day method: three days at home, no diapers, built around her feeling the urge and acting on it. At 30 months she's in a good window. First check she's ready: dry for about 2 hours at a stretch, knows when she's peeing, can sit on the potty and help with her pants. Skip it if she's constipated or a big change is landing. This week, pick 3 clear days at home, put a potty in the room you live in, stock salty snacks and drinks she loves, and get every adult saying the same thing.
value.second: Day 1: bag up the diapers together - "You're done with diapers. Pee and poop go in the potty." Bare from the waist down, lots of fluids and salty snacks. The moment pee starts, carry her to the potty mid-stream and celebrate whatever lands. Say "Tell me when you need to go," not "Do you need to go?" Naps and night stay in a pull-up. Accidents get the same flat, warm line every time: "You peed on the floor. Pee goes in the potty. Let's clean up together." Never scold. Day 2: same, then one 20-40 minute outing after a successful pee, in loose pants with no underwear.
value.third: Day 3: repeat with a longer outing, and prompt at transitions - waking, before leaving, before meals. Expect pees in the potty with prompting, not "done"; accidents run for weeks and poop usually lags. If nothing has landed by the end of day 3 or she's panicking, go back to diapers cheerfully and retry in 4-6 weeks. Call the doctor if she goes 3+ days without pooping or poops hurt.
